name: Indiana

windshield.strip: No AS-1 or strip exception in the statute; the windshield is subject to the same 30% transmittance / 25% reflectance limits as the front side windows
windshield.reflective: max 25% total solar reflectance of visible light (measured on nonfilm side)

frontSide.note: applies to 'side wing' and 'side window that is part of a front door'

backSide.note: rear-door side windows are not listed in § 9-19-19-4(c)

tint.measuredHow: not stated (statute speaks of the window 'covered by or treated with sunscreening material or ... tinted with material' having 30% transmittance)

reflectivity.front: max 25% (windshield, side wings, front-door windows, rear window)
reflectivity.back: not regulated for rear-door side windows

tint.certificateOrSticker: Factory tinting complying with FMVSS 205: proof from the manufacturer, supplier or installer must be carried in the vehicle (§ 9-19-19-4(a)). No installer sticker requirement found.

medicalExemption.text: Driver of a vehicle owned by, or habitually carrying, a person required for medical reasons to be shielded from the sun. Reasons attested by a physician or optometrist licensed in Indiana; certificate carried in the vehicle and renewed annually. Installer may tint for a person who submits that statement.

penalty.text: Driving with non-compliant tint: Class C infraction (§ 9-19-19-7). Tinting a vehicle in violation (installer): Class A infraction (§ 9-19-19-8). Class C infraction judgment up to $500 (IC 34-28-5-4, not re-read).

tint.lastAmended: 2018 (P.L.164-2018, SEC.9; history line of IC 9-19-19-4 in the Indiana Code 2025)
quotes: that is covered by or treated with sunscreening material or is tinted with material that has a total solar reflectance of visible light of more than twenty-five percent (25%) as measured on the nonfilm side and light transmittance of less than thirty percent (30%) in the visible light range.
(1) windshield; (2) side wing; (3) side window that is part of a front door; or (4) rear back window;
The medical reasons must be attested to by a physician or optometrist licensed to practice in Indiana ... The physician's or optometrist's certificate must be renewed annually.
Except as provided in section 8 of this chapter, a person who violates this chapter commits a Class C infraction.
A person who violates section 4(e) of this chapter commits a Class A infraction.

helmet.conditions: Under 18 (operator or passenger) must wear a helmet and eye protection (IC 9-19-7-1); motorcycle learner's permit holders must wear a helmet (IC 9-24-8-3)

studdedTires.season: Oct 1 - May 1 (retractable studs allowed year-round if retracted May 2 - Sep 30)

radarDetector.note: No state ban on radar detectors in private passenger vehicles found; commercial vehicles over 10,001 lb banned federally (49 CFR 392.71)

openQuestions: Tint, helmet (IC 9-19-7-1), phone (IC 9-21-8-59) and studs (IC 9-19-18-3) read on 2026-10-24 in the official Indiana Code 2025 PDF (iga.in.gov/ic/2025/Title_9.pdf).
Underglow and lift/frame height: no Indiana statute located.
Novice/under-21 phone rule not verified on an official page (left null).
